text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for /v1/generate (continuous-batching path). p95 also degraded. Auto-page to #incidents and paging list. Severity: SLO-High :rotating_light:

alex.k: paging oncall — I'm seeing p99 jump to ~1.8s from baseline 300ms. Streaming requests showing stalls/long tails.

maria.g: confirmed on dashboard. p95 ~420ms -> 900ms. p99 ~1.8s -> 2.3s. Error rate stable. No clear CPU/GPU saturation on the host pool.

sam.t: looks like continuous-batcher queue depth spiked on a subset of hosts. Mixed sequence-length histogram skewed to long tails in the last 20m.

jen.w: any customer-facing impact? Do we have customer pages or support tickets?

pm_tom: support reports one customer experiencing slow inference in production (chat app). Not yet widespread, but ticket linked: https://redwood/support/INC-8421

alex.k: quick triage plan: 1) isolate batcher hosts with high tail latency, 2) disable continuous-batching pack-combine on the affected shard (reduce max_pack_size), 3) route new traffic to dedicated small-batch pool as fallback.

maria.g: running query to find affected hosts -> `select host, p99_latency, avg_batch_size from perf.metrics where service='continuous-batcher' and ts > now() - 30m order by p99_latency desc limit 20;`

sam.t: output fragment:
```
host-27a: p99=2300ms avg_batch=11.6
host-12c: p99=2100ms avg_batch=10.9
host-53b: p99=1900ms avg_batch=12.2
```

lia.m: those hosts show higher mixed-seqlen variance too (percentiles skewed). Likely padding amplification causing big KV cache footprint + preemption.

ops-bot: Deploy pipeline report: no config rollouts in last 30m. Autoscaler reports normal.

jen.w: can we try reducing `max_batch_size` on those hosts to 4-6 and enable strict fairshare scheduling to prevent long sequences from monopolizing?

alex.k: I'm going to push a temporary packer override on host-27a and host-12c: reduce max_pack_size=5 and enable early-shed for long sequences. Applying now.

maria.g: also toggling `prefer_streaming_for_seqlen_gt=1024` flag so exceptionally long requests bypass cont-batcher and go to streaming pool.

sam.t: commands I'm running: 
```
redwoodctl nodes patch host-27a --set continuous_batch.max_pack_size=5
redwoodctl nodes patch host-12c --set continuous_batch.max_pack_size=5
redwoodctl nodes patch --label shard=contbatch-east --set scheduler.fairness_mode=strict
```

(10m later)

sam.t: quick update: hosts accepted config change. avg_batch_size on host-27a dropped to 5.6. p99 trending down.

maria.g: Dashboard: p99 decreased from 2.3s -> 1.1s in 6 minutes. p95 now ~480ms. Still above baseline but improving.

pm_tom: support notified customer about mitigation and we're tracking. They report some improvement but intermittent slow messages.

jen.w: any downstream side-effects? Batching reduction can increase cost/lower throughput. We should watch overall throughput and request queueing.

lia.m: checking KV cache eviction stats — eviction rate increased slightly after pack-size drop (expected), but no KB-level OOMs.

alex.k: I'm going to open short-term fallback: route 25% of incoming traffic for that model to dedicated small-batch pool (dedicated-gpu-small) for the next 30m to reduce pressure while we stabilize.

ops-bot: Routing change submitted: traffic-split updated (contbatch: 75%, dedicated-small: 25%). Change id: r-9921.

sam.t: after routing change p99 for cont-batch path is now ~850ms. Overall API p99 ~650ms.

maria.g: impact assessment: ~3 customers saw elevated p99 > 1.5s during peak. One customer reported user-visible slowdowns (chat lag). No failures or errors. No data loss.

pm_tom: drafting customer comms: "We've identified a tail-latency issue impacting a small subset of requests. We've applied mitigations (batch sizing and routing) and are monitoring. We'll follow up with RCA and timelines."

jen.w: next steps for oncall: monitor for 1 hour, leave routing change and pack-size override in place, then attempt gradual rollback to baseline pack_size and traffic split once p99 stable < 400ms for 15m. Also capture traces for affected request ids for postmortem.

lia.m: saving traces and sample request ids: `trace: 0a3f... , 1b7e... , 2c9d...` stored in traces/incident-3398765432.

sam.t: note for RCA: investigate scheduler fairness algorithm under mixed sequence length—looks like long sequences cause padding amplification and KV cache evictions that increase per-token latency for co-batched shorter requests. Consider heuristics to enforce max padding ratio or prefer streaming fallback earlier.

alex.k: handoff to next oncall in 40m @sam.t (next shift). Current state: mitigations in place, p99 trending down ~650ms, dedicated-small handling 25% traffic, no errors. Action items: 1) monitor, 2) capture traces, 3) evaluate any rollbacks -> sam.t will take postmortem.

sam.t: ack. I'll take the handoff and continue monitoring for 2h. Will start an RCA doc and tag research/eng-ml for scheduler/kv investigation.

pm_tom: I'll update the support ticket and add a customer-facing note.

incident-bot: NOTE: Escalation window closed by alex.k. Incident severity downgraded to SLO-Medium at 3398766000.

jen.w: thanks all. If anything regresses, ping me and escalate immediately.

sam.t: handoff summary (copy for next shift): mitigations applied (pack_size=5 on bad hosts, prefer_streaming_for_seqlen_gt=1024, traffic split to dedicated-small 25%), sample traces collected, customer notified. Next: RCA focused on padding amplification + scheduler fairness + potential early streaming routing.

lia.m: adding runbook note: consider exposing `max_padding_ratio` and early-streaming threshold as runtime knobs for quick mitigations next time.

pm_tom: closing loop with support: customer will be kept posted; ETA for RCA initial findings: ~24-48h.

end of thread.
